name: Wall Ball
description: Wall ball is a functional conditioning exercise in which the athlete performs a full squat holding a medicine ball and then uses the momentum of the squat ascent to propel the ball upward and throw it against a target on a wall, catching the rebounding ball to begin the next squat. It trains the full lower body squat pattern combined with an explosive upper body press in a continuous, high-intensity movement pattern, making it a staple of functional fitness conditioning workouts.

execution.starting_position: Stand facing a wall at approximately 1 meter distance, holding the medicine ball at chin height with both hands.
execution.setup_instructions: Mark a target on the wall at the prescribed height (typically 3 meters for men, 2.7 meters for women in functional fitness standards). Use a soft medicine ball rated for wall-ball impact.
steps: Step 1: Hold the ball at chest/chin height, stand facing the wall.
Step 2: Descend into a full squat — hip crease below the knee.
Step 3: Drive out of the squat explosively, transferring momentum into the arms.
Step 4: Push the ball upward and release it toward the wall target.
Step 5: Catch the ball as it rebounds and absorb into the next squat immediately.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale sharply at the top of the throw. Inhale on the descent.
common_mistakes: Not reaching full squat depth — the hip crease must pass below the knee
Throwing too early — the throw should be powered by the leg drive, not the arms alone
Catching the ball with straight arms — absorb with slightly bent elbows
safety_considerations: Missing the catch can result in the ball dropping on the face or head — stay alert throughout.
Adequate shoulder mobility for the overhead throw position.
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full squat depth. Full overhead extension at ball release.
execution.tempo_recommendations: Performed for reps (10–30) or time (60–120 second intervals) in conditioning workouts.
coaching_cues: Squat deep — hip crease below the knee
Drive up — throw at the top
